title: Redis is Single-Threaded: How it Serves 100K Req/Sec

instagram_meta.caption:
Redis runs on a single CPU core, yet it outpaces multithreaded databases ten times its size.

Redis avoids multithreading because mutex lock contention and thread context switching kill performance. Instead, it uses Linux epoll I/O multiplexing. A single non-blocking event loop handles thousands of concurrent socket connections entirely in L3 cache without a single thread lock.

In low-latency memory systems, avoiding lock contention is faster than throwing 64 CPU cores at the problem.

title: Big-O Time Complexity: Why O(N²) Destroys Production

instagram_meta.caption:
The difference between O(1) and O(N²) is the difference between 1 millisecond and 30,000 years.

For 1,000 items, an O(N) algorithm runs 1,000 operations. But an O(N²) nested loop runs 1 million operations. At 1 million items, O(N) takes 1 millisecond, while O(N²) takes 1 trillion operations — freezing your server forever.

Always replace nested loops with Hash Maps to transform O(N²) operations into O(1) lookups.

title: False Sharing: The Hardware Glitch Killing Multithreading

instagram_meta.caption:
You added 8 CPU threads to make your program faster, and it ran ten times slower. Here is why.

CPUs do not read single bytes from RAM; they fetch 64-byte chunks called Cache Lines. If Thread 1 on Core 0 modifies Variable A, and Thread 2 on Core 1 modifies independent Variable B right next to it, the hardware invalidates the entire cache line across all cores via MESI protocol.

The CPU cores spend 95% of their time fighting over cache coherence buses instead of doing actual computation.

title: Why Roman Concrete Gets Stronger Over 2,000 Years

instagram_meta.caption:
Ancient Roman harbors have been battered by ocean waves for 2,000 years — and they are harder today than when they were built.

MIT geologists discovered Romans mixed quicklime at extreme temperatures, leaving microscopic lime clasts. When seawater cracks the concrete, it dissolves the lime, precipitating calcium carbonate that literally heals the cracks in real time.

Modern concrete crumbles in 50 years, but ancient Roman chemistry engineered self-healing stone that outlives empires.
